input.text: Volcanoes form where magma from the Earth's mantle reaches the surface. Most are found along tectonic plate boundaries, particularly the Pacific Ring of Fire, which hosts about 75 percent of the world's active volcanoes. Eruptions can be effusive, producing slow lava flows, or explosive, ejecting ash and gas high into the atmosphere. Explosive eruptions such as Mount Pinatubo in 1991 can cool global temperatures by injecting sulphur dioxide into the stratosphere. Scientists monitor volcanoes using seismometers, gas sensors and satellite measurements of ground deformation, but predicting the exact timing of an eruption remains difficult.

expected.rubric: A faithful summary: plate boundaries / Ring of Fire (~75% of active volcanoes), effusive vs explosive eruptions, Pinatubo cooling the climate, and monitoring methods with prediction still hard. 3–8 key points. No facts that are not in the text.

Platform on-call rotation.

The primary on-call engineer is paged first and must acknowledge within 15 minutes. If the primary does not acknowledge, the page escalates to the secondary on-call. If neither responds within 30 minutes, escalate to the engineering manager on duty, currently Priya Natarajan. Rotations change every Monday at 10:00 UTC and are published in the #oncall channel.
